title: I Built My Pottery Studio a Real Booking Website (I Can't Code)
creator: Rosa Delgado
description:
For two years every single class booking at the studio went through my Instagram DMs and a very sad spreadsheet. This week I finally fixed that.

Thanks to Tessera for sponsoring part of this video. The site in this video was built on Tessera.

Thursday wheel classes, open studio hours and glaze nights are all bookable now at the link in my bio.

Music: Epidemic Sound
Filmed on a phone propped on a bag of clay, as usual.

sentences.t: Okay, so if you've ever tried to book a class at my studio, first of all, I'm sorry.
Because for two years the whole system has been me, my Instagram DMs, and a spreadsheet that my sister calls the crime scene.
Like, I had people double booked on the same wheel, I had someone show up for a glaze night that I cancelled in March, it was bad.
And every Sunday night I'm sitting here with clay under my nails going through forty messages going, wait, did I say yes to her?
So this week the goal is simple, the studio gets a real website where people can see the classes, pick a spot, and pay, and I never touch the spreadsheet again.
I'm building it in Tessera, who are actually sponsoring this part of the video, so thank you Tessera, genuinely good timing.
So I'm in the template picker right now and, okay, there's a lot of very beige candle shop energy here, which, honestly, kind of my vibe.
I'm going to go with this one called Field because it has a big photo at the top and the class list right under it.
First thing, I'm dragging in my own photos, this is the kiln on firing day, and this is Thursday group from last month, everybody's covered in slip.
You just drop it on the block and it crops it for you, which, okay, it cut off Marcus's head, so let me just drag that down a bit.
There, Marcus lives.
Now the part I actually care about, which is the booking calendar.
I'm adding a block called Classes, and it asks me for the class name, so, Thursday Wheel, six to eight thirty, and the price.
And here's the thing I wanted, there's a capacity setting, so I'm putting in eight, because I have eight wheels, and the ninth person just gets a waitlist instead of me apologizing in the DMs.
I'm doing the same for open studio and glaze night, and for glaze night I'm turning on this reminder email that goes out the day before, because people forget, I forget.
Then payments, I'm just connecting the card reader account I already use at the studio, it found it right away, which I did not expect.
Okay, let's preview it on the phone, because nobody is booking a pottery class from a laptop, let's be real.
Yeah, the class list stacks nicely, the button is big, my mom could do this.
I'm changing the button text from Book Now to Grab a Wheel because that's more me, and, publish.
Oh my gosh, it's live.
So I sent the link to the Thursday group chat and I'm just going to wedge some clay while I wait and see if anyone actually uses it.
This is reclaim, by the way, it's all the scraps from last week, you wedge it like this to push the air bubbles out so nothing explodes in the kiln.
If you've ever heard a pop in a kiln, that's someone's mug that had an air pocket, and it takes out the mug next to it too, so this matters.
Okay, my phone just buzzed.
Priya booked Thursday, and then Dev, and then, oh, three people booked glaze night in like two minutes, I am going to cry.
Nobody messaged me, nobody asked if there was room, they just saw the spots and took them.
The one thing I'd change is I want to put a little note on the Thursday class saying wear clothes you don't love, because people still show up in white jeans.
Anyway, the spreadsheet is officially retired, I'm going to print it out and fire it in the kiln as a ceremony, I'm kidding, paper doesn't really work like that.
Next week I want to try throwing the big serving bowls for the studio sale, which I have failed at four times on camera, so that should be fun.
Thanks for hanging out with me, go make something with your hands, and I'll see you next week.
